supporting_observations.claim: WS-BCARTER-01 made multiple connections to the explicit proxy during the review window. The available proxy record identifies a CONNECT to update.chartmate-imaging.net at 14:10 UTC; the listed approved ChartMate domain is update.chartmate-imaging.com.

The 14:10 proxy connection to update.chartmate-imaging.net is associated with cmupdate.exe running from Ben Carter's AppData\Local\ChartMate directory, rather than the approved inventory path under Program Files. This domain and path mismatch is suspicious, but does not by itself prove malicious execution.

Dropbox.exe was launched by ben.carter from Explorer on WS-BCARTER-01. Dropbox is an unapproved file-sharing service in the supplied environment context; the launch establishes use of the client, not that files were uploaded.
A file named installer-70930.exe was created in Ben Carter's Downloads folder, but the available record does not establish its source, contents, or whether it was executed.

Authentication records show WS-BCARTER-01 associated with network logons involving maria.lopez on WS-MLOPEZ-01 and omar.haddad on WS-OHADDAD-01. These cross-host authentication events merit investigation, but do not establish who initiated them or whether the credentials were misused.

known_telemetry_limitations: The Zeek records show connections to the explicit proxy, but most do not identify the tunneled destination; only the 14:10 proxy CONNECT record supplies a hostname. The available records therefore cannot attribute the other proxy flows to a particular application or service. (T025-00058, T025-00096, T025-00102, T025-00294)
The proxy CONNECT record reports tunnel byte counts, but the provided evidence does not expose the HTTPS contents or identify any files transferred. (T025-00294)
The records establish Dropbox process launch but provide no Dropbox network connection or transfer record in the supplied window. (T025-00326, T025-00328)
The provided process and authentication events do not establish the user's intent, the origin of installer-70930.exe, or whether it was run. (T025-00341)
claims_not_established: Whether the repeated proxy connections were actually to an external command-and-control service, to ChartMate, or to another destination; the provided records identify a hostname for only one CONNECT. (T025-00058, T025-00096, T025-00102, T025-00294)
Whether the .net ChartMate hostname and AppData-based cmupdate.exe are unauthorized or malicious rather than an undocumented legitimate deployment. (T025-00294, T025-00296, T025-00297)
Whether Dropbox uploaded, downloaded, or synchronized organizational data. (T025-00326, T025-00328)
Whether installer-70930.exe is malicious or was executed. (T025-00341)
Whether the cross-host authentication events represent unauthorized lateral movement or legitimate activity. (T025-00012, T025-00013, T025-00062, T025-00063)
additional_evidence_needed: Obtain full proxy logs for the review window, including CONNECT destinations, user-agent details, byte counts, and any available request or destination metadata.

Determine the signer, hash, origin, and installation history of C:\Users\ben.carter\AppData\Local\ChartMate\cmupdate.exe; compare them with a verified ChartMate release and confirm the correct update domain.
Collect endpoint network telemetry for Dropbox.exe and relevant file-system or cloud-sync records to determine whether data was transferred.
Acquire installer-70930.exe and its download provenance, hash, signature, and execution history.
Correlate the maria.lopez and omar.haddad authentication events with source-side logon/process records and validate them with the involved users or administrators.
